text.p: Stocks slid on profit-taking Thursday, giving up some of this week's stunning gains built on Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's upbeat comments about the economy.
At 1 p.m. EDT (1700 GMT), the 30-stock Dow Jones industrial average was off 58.07 points at 8,030.29.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 16-10 on active volume of 323 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index was off 5.85 points at 1,561.80.

"It's nothing but profit-taking," said John Cleland, chief investment strategist at Security Benefit Group of Cos. "We get these huge run-ups in a day or two, then people start to take some profits out of the market."

The Dow rose 155 points Tuesday and added another 27 points Wednesday after Greenspan, in congressional testimony, talked of the economy's continued moderate growth with no current signs of inflation, soothing any worries about an imminent interest rate increase.
The profit-taking was widespread and came despite solid corporate earnings announcements.

"There are still some investors who are concerned about valuations," said Robert Froelich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds. "These declines are certainly not driven by earnings disappointments or inflation concerns."
Analysts said most quarterly earnings have come in as forecast or higher than Wall Street estimates, providing support for the stock markets.

Digital Equipment Corp. reported a profit of 75 cents a share compared with a loss of $2.87 per share in the year-ago quarter. The company also said its board authorised the repurchase of up to 15 million shares. Digital gained 1-3/8 to 41-3/8.
Colgate-Palmolive Co. said it earned 58 cents per share vs. 49 cents a year ago, surpassing analysts' estimates of 56 cents a share. Its stock gained 1/16 to 75-7/16.
AirTouch Communications Inc. surged after reporting profits of 21 cents per share, higher than Wall Street's estimate of 14 cents a share.
"Earnings reports have been very good," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
Delta Air Lines lost 11/16 to 87-1/2, after the company posted disappointing results.
Mallinckrodt Inc. lost 1-1/4 at 38-1/2 on news that it was acquiring medical product supplier Nellcor Puritan Bennett Inc. for $1.9 billion. Nellcor rose 7-1/8 to 28-1/16.
